### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **2** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-defaults/ai.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx`  _(via azure_openai (literal, a string literal in AIModelConfigSchema))_
- `content/docs/ai/index.mdx`  _(via azure_openai (literal, a string literal in AIModelConfigSchema))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-defaults/ai.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **177** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 579b85776d1abb6722df870eb2a652231ee4047e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8e35a80aa656d584f7a0fe00e097d769a3b363b4` — the merge of head `2241d53bae9e432bf558f61d241a77255e154618` into base `579b85776d1abb6722df870eb2a652231ee4047e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8e35a80aa656d584f7a0fe00e097d769a3b363b4 && git checkout 8e35a80aa656d584f7a0fe00e097d769a3b363b4
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 579b85776d1abb6722df870eb2a652231ee4047e 2241d53bae9e432bf558f61d241a77255e154618 && git checkout -B drift-repro 579b85776d1abb6722df870eb2a652231ee4047e && git merge --no-ff 2241d53bae9e432bf558f61d241a77255e154618

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 579b85776d1abb6722df870eb2a652231ee4047e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 579b85776d1abb6722df870eb2a652231ee4047e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d36940ae4ba86aac90b8223334d50290e21a1dbd`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ai/agent.zod.ts + none
Security-touching: no
Rule-change-verified: none

Read: card #37686 (body, 3 comments), PR #37697 (body, 4 files, net diff against `main`, merge-base `6d106a1a`), the 74 check-runs on this head. The rest of the diff (`agent.test.ts`, the regenerated `content/docs/references/ai/agent.mdx`, the changeset) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`; no file in the diff implements or enforces the hits file beyond those.

Gates, read off the head's check-runs (latest completed run per name): 0 failure. `Check Changeset` has two runs, failure at 21:07:54Z (pre-edit PR body) and success at 21:08:15Z; the later one counts. `Spec property liveness`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, the `Lint` and `Type Check` families (including `Type Check · consumer gates`), `Test Core` 1-10 and `Test UI` 1-16 are success; the skipped runs are opt-in or queue-only jobs.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept-set of `AIModelConfigSchema`: a block with no `model` key now parses (`{}`, `{ temperature: 0.2 }`). Right: this is the ruling (「框架允许省略 model」) and the card's first acceptance line.
- Everything accepted before is still accepted, with the same parsed value: `model` stays `z.string()` inside the optional, so `{ model: 'x' }` is carried as written. Right.
- Still refused: a non-string `model` (`4`, `null`; the field is optional, not nullable), and any unknown key (the block is still `strictObject`). Right: no accept-set growth beyond the one the ruling names.
- No sentinel value and no tier key added. Right (card step 3).
- Parsed output of a model-less block: `model` is `undefined`, `provider` is still defaulted to `'openai'`, `temperature` to `0.7`. The `model` part is right; the `provider` default on a block that names no model is S1 below.
- `AgentSchema.model` (the block itself) is unchanged: still `AIModelConfigSchema.optional()`. Right.
- Public TypeScript surface: `Agent` (`z.input`) and `AgentParsed` (`z.infer`) both move `model.model` from `string` to `string | undefined` (input: the key becomes optional). There is no exported `AIModelConfig` type (`docs-import-surface.baseline.json`: "no type export"), so the change reaches consumers through `Agent`/`AgentParsed` and `z.infer` of `AIModelConfigSchema` alone. This is source-affecting for a TypeScript reader that assigns `agent.model.model` to a `string`; it is the unavoidable consequence of the ruling, the changeset's "What to do" paragraph states it, and `Type Check · consumer gates` and `Type Check · workspace` are green on this head. Right.
- Generated surface: the key set is unchanged, so `authorable-surface`, `authorable-defaults`, `api-surface`, the JSON-schema manifest and the metadata-form translations (which carry only the `model.model` label) owe no change; the one stale artefact, `agent.mdx`, is regenerated and now reads `optional` / `model?: string`. Right, and the generated-artefact gates are green.
- List column `model.model` (`metadata-list-registry.ts:203`, outside the diff): answers `undefined`, an empty cell, for an agent with no model name. Right against the card's "empty/default" wording.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec: minor`. The diff relaxes a requirement an author had to meet, which is a newly accepted value: `Metadata-protocol: added`, and that kind takes at least `minor` on the package the diff moves (AGENTS.md, changeset rule). The level matches what the diff publishes.

Clause-②: yes (widening) — present line-initial in both the PR body and the changeset body, and it is the correct arm: nothing accepted before is refused now. The claim comment on the card still reads `Clause-②: no`; the dev report records the correction as a deviation and the later `Check Changeset` run accepts the corrected pair. No BREAKING banner or ADR-0087 disposition is owed for a widening.

### ③ Boundary flags

- PR author login: `objectstack-fleet[bot]`. Nothing to note.
- Dev flag, `model.provider` declared but not enforced: confirmed by reading. In this repo no runtime reads an agent's `model.provider` (only `AgentPreview.tsx:156` displays it); in cloud `origin/main` `585b04a`, `agent-runtime.ts:1027-1030` reads `model`, `temperature` and `maxTokens` from the block and nothing else. The card (step 4) says note it, do not remove it here; the dev did exactly that. ESCALATED to the seat, carrier objectstack-ai/cloud#5055: it is an ADR-0049 enforce-or-remove candidate, and S1 below is a reason to settle it before phase 2 rather than after.
- Dev flag, Skills-docs follow-up owed: confirmed. `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md:365` cites `packages/spec/src/ai/agent.zod.ts:36-40` (the field now sits at 38-42) and teaches `model` as a required free string; `skills/objectstack-ai/evals/skills-tools-knowledge.json:17` expects "a free-string `model`". `skills/**` is outside this card's fence, so `follow-up owed` is the right value and the PR-body guards accept it. ESCALATED to the seat: the follow-up card is owed on a `domain:skills` path, and until it lands the skill teaches authors and AI to invent a model name, the exact behaviour the ruling removes.
- Dev deviation, no reviewer requested and the relay trailer on the PR body: process notes, no contract effect.
- Open questions: the dev report carries none.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. The diff contains no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join.
- Security: no changed hunk teaches permission, credential, token or authentication behaviour.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/ai/agent.zod.ts`, against the ruling (agent `model.model` optional; absent = environment default model) and its first consumer.

Attempts to break it:

- Strictness. The block is still built by `strictObject`; `{ temperature: 0.2, tier: 'fast' }` is refused as `unrecognized_keys`. Making `model` optional does not open a silent-strip path.
- Aliases. `modelName`, `llm`, `deployment`, `engine` → `model` are suggestion hints for the unknown-key error, not input mappings. Before this change `{ llm: 'gpt-4o' }` failed twice (missing `model`, unknown `llm`); now it fails once, on `llm`, with the "did you mean `model`" prescription. The dangerous outcome, a misspelled model key silently parsing as "use the default", cannot happen while the block is strict. Holds.
- Defaults. No default was added for `model`, so absent stays absent through parse; a default would have been a sentinel by another name. Holds.
- Null and wrong types. `.optional()` and not `.nullish()`: `model: null` and `model: 4` are refused. Holds.
- Description and form generation. The description is on the optional wrapper and reaches the generated reference table; the key set is unchanged, so form and translation generation are unaffected.
- First consumer, cloud `origin/main` `585b04a`, `packages/service-ai/src/agent-runtime.ts:1027-1030`: `options.model = agent.model.model` assigns into `AIRequestOptions.model?: string`; cloud does not set `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, so the assignment type-checks with `string | undefined`. At runtime an absent name leaves `options.model` undefined; `agent-routes.ts:1098-1099` then writes the chosen or default model id over it, and `selectRequestModelId` (`vercel-adapter.ts:505`) maps an undefined or blank want to the boot default. So "absent = environment default" already holds end to end at the consumer, and cloud card objectstack-ai/cloud#5059 (user pick, then agent `model.model`, then default) can read `undefined` as "the agent declares none" with no further spec change. Holds.
- Other readers that assume a string: `AgentPreview.tsx:156` already guards `model.model ?`; `metadata-list-registry.ts:203` goes through `valueAtPath`. Neither breaks.

Findings:

S1 (should-fix) — not blocking, follow-up: `provider` still defaults to `'openai'` on a block that names no model. `{ temperature: 0.2 }` parses to `{ provider: 'openai', temperature: 0.2 }`, so the parsed agent asserts a provider for a model the host picks, and `AgentPreview.tsx:156` (`model.provider && ...`) shows an `openai` pill for an agent that runs on the environment default, whatever provider that is. The statement was already unenforced for a name-only block; this widening adds the case where it is wrong by construction. Fixing it means changing or removing a default (`Metadata-protocol: semantic` or a retirement), which the card forbids here (step 4). It belongs with the `provider` enforce-or-remove escalation in ③, carrier objectstack-ai/cloud#5055.

N1 (nit) — `model: ''` is still accepted and is now a second spelling of "no model" at the spec level. The first consumer already treats blank as the default (`selectRequestModelId` trims and falls through), so nothing misbehaves; cloud#5059 should compare on truthiness, not on `!== undefined`.

No must-fix.

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `db5f0e7de958b70b1e0102ba62b9077c8912d5a4`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ai/agent.zod.ts + packages/spec/scripts/lib/default-changes.ts, packages/spec/authorable-defaults/ai.json

Delta review: this record supersedes the one on `d36940ae4ba86aac90b8223334d50290e21a1dbd` and covers the whole net diff against `main` (merge-base `6d106a1a`, 6 files), with the delta since that head read hunk by hunk. Read: card #37686 (body, 3 comments, none new since the first record), PR #37697 (body, files, net diff), the 74 check-runs on this head. The rest of the diff (`agent.test.ts`, the regenerated `content/docs/references/ai/agent.mdx`, the changeset) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

Gates, read off this head's check-runs (latest completed run per name): 62 success, 12 skipped, 0 failure. `Check Changeset` has two runs (22:31:26Z and 23:01:08Z), both success. `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Spec property liveness`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, the `Type Check` family (including `Type Check · consumer gates`), `Test Core` and `Test UI` are success; the skipped runs are opt-in or queue-only jobs.

### ① Derived judgments

Carried from the first record and re-read on this head, unchanged and still right: a block with no `model` key parses; an explicit name is carried as written; a non-string or `null` name and any unknown key are refused; no sentinel, no tier key, no default for `model`; `AgentSchema.model` itself is unchanged; `Agent` and `AgentParsed` carry `model.model` as `string | undefined`; the list column answers an empty cell.

New in the delta:

- `provider` goes from `z.enum([...]).default('openai')` to `z.enum([...]).optional()`. Accept-set unchanged: the same four values are accepted, an off-enum value (`'google'`) and `null` are refused, an absent key was and is accepted. Right.
- Parsed value: a block that writes no `provider` now parses with no `provider` key at all (not `'openai'`). This is a default removed from an existing authorable key, which changes what already-written metadata parses to. Right as the fix for S1, and right only because it is declared: see the next two lines.
- `packages/spec/scripts/lib/default-changes.ts`: a `19` bucket with one entry, `ai/AIModelConfig:provider`, `from: '"openai"'`, `to: '(none)'`. `from` equals the baseline line removed from `authorable-defaults/ai.json`; the bucket is the build's own major (`packages/spec/package.json` is `19.0.0-next.0`; `main` has buckets `17` and `18` only); the reason says what a consumer relying on the old value reads now and what to write to keep it. The gate that re-derives `from`/`to` (`check:authorable-surface`) is green in CI. Right.
- `packages/spec/authorable-defaults/ai.json`: the one line `ai/AIModelConfig:provider = "openai"` is dropped, nothing else moves; `temperature = 0.7` stays. Agrees with the schema. Right.
- Public TypeScript surface: `AgentParsed['model']['provider']` (and `z.infer` of `AIModelConfigSchema`) goes from the enum to the enum or `undefined`; the input type `Agent` is unchanged for `provider` (it was already optional on input). Source-affecting for a reader of the parsed type that assumed a value; the changeset and the bucket reason both say so, and `Type Check · consumer gates` and `Type Check · workspace` are green. Right.
- Key set unchanged, so `authorable-surface`, `api-surface`, the JSON-schema manifest and the form translations owe nothing; `agent.mdx` now shows `provider` as plain `optional` in both tables. Right.
- No migration-registry `semantic` entry was added for the default move. Right: the table's own header asks for one when the change warrants a migration TODO, and with no runtime reading `model.provider` there is nothing for an author to migrate.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec: minor`. The diff now carries two protocol kinds: a relaxed requirement (`added`) and a moved default (`semantic`); AGENTS.md ranks `semantic` over `added`, and either kind takes at least `minor` on the package the diff moves. `Metadata-protocol: semantic` is the correct line and the level matches what the diff publishes.

Clause-②: yes (widening) — line-initial in both the PR body and the changeset body, and still the correct arm: no value accepted before is refused now, for either key. The default move is a semantic change to the parsed value, declared in `DEFAULT_CHANGES_BY_MAJOR` and described in the changeset with the one-line way to keep the old value (`provider: 'openai'`); it does not narrow the accept-set, so no `(narrowing)` arm and no BREAKING banner is owed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- PR author login: `objectstack-fleet[bot]`. Nothing to note.
- Dev flag, `model.provider` declared but not enforced: now carried by objectstack-ai/objectstack#37712 (open, enforce-or-remove). Re-read on this head and on cloud `origin/main` `585b04a`: still no runtime reader of an agent's `model.provider` in either repo (`vercel-adapter.ts:391` reads the AI SDK model object, not the agent block). Answered.
- Dev flag, Skills docs: now `Skills-docs: follow-up #37711` (open). The follow-up owes one more line than when it was filed: `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md` also teaches `provider` default `openai`, which this head removes. ESCALATED to the seat: make sure #37711's scope names the dropped default, not only the optional model name.
- Seat amendment of the card's step 4 ("do not remove it here"): the key and its enum are not removed, only the default; the PR body names the amendment. Consistent with the card's fence (`packages/spec/**` plus generated files).
- Dev note, overlap with #37676 (also opens a `19` bucket and touches `authorable-defaults/ai.json`): a textual conflict for whichever lands second, no contract effect; the queue's business.
- Dev note, display consequence in `AgentPreview.tsx`: confirmed, graded S2 below.
- Cloud built-ins: `ask-agent.ts:115` and `metadata-assistant-agent.ts:78` write `provider: 'openai'` explicitly, so they parse identically until cloud#5059 removes the lines.
- Open questions: none carried by the dev report.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. No query, no id materialisation, no in-app join in the diff.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/ai/agent.zod.ts`, against the ruling (agent `model.model` optional; absent = environment default model) and its first consumer; `default-changes.ts` and `authorable-defaults/ai.json` for agreement with it.

- S1: closed — `provider` no longer defaults. `{ temperature: 0.2 }` parses to a block with no `provider` key (the new test asserts `'provider' in result` is false), so the parsed agent no longer asserts a provider for a model the host picks, and `AgentPreview.tsx:156` shows no `openai` pill for it. The fix is the smallest one that removes the false statement: key and enum kept, retirement left to #37712.

Attempts to break the delta:

- A hidden reader that relied on the default. Searched both repos for readers of an agent's `model.provider`: only `AgentPreview.tsx:156` (display). Cloud `agent-runtime.ts:1027-1030` reads `model`, `temperature`, `maxTokens`. Nothing branches on the value, so no deployed agent changes behaviour.
- The default ratchet bypassed rather than satisfied. The entry's `from` matches the baseline, `to` is `(none)` and the baseline line is gone; the bucket is the current major. An entry that did not match would fail `check:authorable-surface`, which is green.
- A provider-only block. `{ provider: 'anthropic' }` parses and means "anthropic, model unnamed": a statement nothing enforces, but one the author wrote, which is #37712's subject, not a defect of this change.
- Strictness, aliases, null handling, form generation: unchanged from the first record and still hold.
- First consumer and cloud#5059: unaffected by the delta; `options.model` handling is as judged before, and cloud#5059's removal of the built-ins' `provider`/`model` lines now yields a block with neither, which is what that card wants.
- `default-changes.ts` and `authorable-defaults/ai.json` agree with the schema line for line.

Findings:

S2 (should-fix) — not blocking, follow-up outside this card's fence: `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/AgentPreview.tsx:156` gates the whole model pill on `model.provider`. With the default gone, an agent that writes a model name and no provider (`model: { model: 'gpt-4o' }`) loses its pill entirely, so the preview no longer shows the model NAME, where it showed `openai · gpt-4o`. The invented provider is rightly gone; the name going with it is a display regression this change causes in a file it may not touch (`ui/**`). #37712 names the preview but not this consequence. ## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b3238ea812f4d8e6bb609f5533cc40d801045a9f`

The rest of the diff (`agent.test.ts`, `AgentPreview.test.tsx`, the regenerated `content/docs/references/ai/agent.mdx`, the changeset) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

Gates, read off this head's check-runs (latest completed run per name): 63 success, 11 skipped, 0 failure. `Check Changeset` has two runs (23:11:05Z and 23:37:09Z), both success. `Lint UI`, `Type Check UI`, `Test UI`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, the `Lint` and `Type Check` families and `Test Core` are success; the skipped runs are opt-in or queue-only jobs.

### ① Derived judgments

Carried from the two earlier records, re-read on this head, unchanged and still right:

- A block with no `model` key parses; an explicit name is carried as written; a non-string or `null` name and any unknown key are refused; no sentinel, no tier key, no default for `model`.
- `provider` is `z.enum([...]).optional()` with no default: same four values accepted, off-enum and `null` refused, and a block that writes none parses with no `provider` key.
- The default move is declared in `default-changes.ts` under `19` (`from: '"openai"'`, `to: '(none)'`; the package is at `19.0.0-next.0`) and `authorable-defaults/ai.json` drops exactly that line.
- `Agent` and `AgentParsed` carry `model.model` as `string | undefined`; `AgentParsed['model']['provider']` is the enum or `undefined`.
- Key set unchanged, so the surface, api-surface, manifest and translation artefacts owe nothing.

New in this delta:

- `AgentPreview.tsx`: the model pill renders when `model.provider` or `model.model` is set (was: `provider` alone), and its label is `[provider, model].filter(Boolean).join(' · ')`. The four cases: both written reads `openai · gpt-4o`, byte-identical to before; name only reads `gpt-4o`; provider only reads `anthropic`, as before; neither shows no pill. Right: the preview now states exactly what the author wrote and gives the environment default no name.
- An empty string in either key is falsy on both the condition and the filter, so `model: ''` shows no pill and no stray separator. Right, and consistent with the first consumer treating a blank name as the default.
- No new i18n key, no new prop, no change to the preview's public signature; the local `ModelConfig` interface already declared both keys optional. Right.
- No spec file moved in this delta (`agent.zod.ts`, `default-changes.ts`, `authorable-defaults/ai.json` are identical to `db5f0e7d`). Right.
